rationale: The available literature demonstrates that seizures and epilepsy are variable, non-core features of Popov-Chang syndrome (YWHAZ-related neurodevelopmental disorder) rather than a defining refractory epileptic encephalopathy. In a large three-generation family carrying the pathogenic YWHAZ c.147A>T (p.Lys49Asn) variant, Wan et al. (2023) observed that febrile seizures and epilepsy were not a common feature among affected individuals. Phenotype databases (such as FindZebra) similarly catalog seizures only as an inconsistent, variable finding alongside short stature and dysmorphic features. No counter-evidence in the provided literature identifies Popov-Chang syndrome as presenting with classical or high-frequency refractory epileptic encephalopathy (HP:0200134). However, the specific '<15%' quantitative threshold lacks systematic multi-cohort numerator and denominator data in the provided excerpted text.

evidence.text: In a study analyzing a large three-generation family with a pathogenic YWHAZ missense variant (p.Lys49Asn) causing intellectual disability and global developmental delay, epilepsy or febrile seizures were determined not to be common clinical features.

source.title: YWHAZ variation causes intellectual disability and global developmental delay
source.quote: This indicated that febrile seizure or epilepsy should not be a common feature in this large three-generation family with the YWHAZ variation.

evidence.text: Popov-Chang syndrome is characterized by intellectual disability, developmental delay, and facial dysmorphism, with seizures documented only as highly variable secondary features rather than an obligate or predominant presentation.

source.title: Popov-Chang Syndrome
source.quote: Additional features are highly variable and can include seizures, short stature, feeding difficulties, and skin abnormalities

evidence.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) represent early-onset disorders defined by severe refractory seizures and developmental arrest or regression; more than 50% of DEE cases remain genetically unsolved.

source.title: Recent advances in epilepsy genomics and genetic testing
source.quote: However, more than 50% of patients with DEE remain without a genetic diagnosis despite state-of-the-art genetic testing.

numbers.metric: Percentage of DEE patients without genetic diagnosis

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence, electroclinical syndromic classification, and pharmacosensitivity of seizures across all published YWHAZ/Popov-Chang syndrome probands?
new_directions.rationale: Existing sources establish that seizures are inconsistent, but precise cohort denominators and HPO-level documentation of epileptic encephalopathy versus non-encephalopathic seizures remain uncompiled.

new_directions.question_text: Does the phenotypic spectrum of YWHAZ variants correlate with functional domain alterations (e.g., phosphopeptide binding groove vs. dimerization interface) in determining seizure propensity?
new_directions.rationale: Differences in missense variant location or dominant-negative versus haploinsufficiency mechanisms could explain why rare individuals experience seizures while large pedigrees lack epilepsy.
